To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CRM success depends on the alignment of organizational capabilities and the CRM system, the alignment between the CRM system and the business model and the ability of the CRM system to support the business model.
CRM is a complex and risky innovation.

CRM success is a function of: (1) the ability to identify and target customers who will benefit from a CRM initiative; (2) the ability to implement CRM systems in a way that will deliver the benefits expected; (3) the ability to manage customer interactions in a way that maximizes customer value; (4) the ability to develop and maintain a customer-focused culture within the organization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How can managers use simulation to understand better the factors that lead to success and failure in CRM implementation?
understanding the underlying dynamics that drive CRM success and failure and how these can be managed.
understanding the factors which influence the success of CRM implementation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CRM is a complex innovation which requires careful management of a number of interrelated factors if success is to be achieved.
CRM success and failure are determined by the interaction of many factors, including the organization, the technology, the users and the environment.

the success of CRM implementation depends on a number of factors including organizational support for the initiative, the benefits that the organization hopes to gain and the level of customer satisfaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a dynamic model that can be used to simulate the innovation process in CRM and that the simulation results are in agreement with previous research on CRM success.
we are able to identify some of the underlying causes of failure in CRM implementation.
CRM systems can be a powerful tool in the hands of a company.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the success of a CRM implementation is a function of the interaction of a number of factors, including the characteristics of the technology, the organization, the implementation process, the implementation context, and the user.

the benefits of CRM are not realized immediately, but accrue over time as the system becomes embedded into the organization's business processes. This means that organizations should not expect to see the full benefits of CRM immediately
the benefits of CRM are likely to increase over time, but that this increase is dependent on a number of factors.
